note:
Measured 2026-07-31 from the first working reference and implementation across all twenty Golden cases, then reviewed and committed. A tolerance is an input to validation, not an output of it.

The oracle and the port both run F32 on CPU, so these thresholds carry neither a dtype nor a device difference -- only an implementation one -- and are accordingly far tighter than qwen3-tts's. The deep generator probes gate on cosine; the two waveform probes gate on cosine AND max-abs, because a listener hears the waveform and a cosine over it would hide a constant offset.

Every cosine threshold is five times the measured deviation in (1 - cosine), rounded DOWN to six decimals -- the precision the qwen3-tts file already uses. At this family's scale that rounding is not cosmetic and the file says so rather than repeating a clean '5x': the measured deviations run from 9.06e-08 to 2.14e-07, so the committed gates land at 1e-06 (2e-06 at hidden_l27), which is between 5.1x and 11.0x the measured figure. Rounding the other way would tighten past the rule.

There is a second reason not to cut finer, and it is the more important one. The cosine estimate is computed in float32 over arrays of 24k to 6.7M elements, and on these same runs it returns cosines ABOVE 1.0 by as much as 2.08e-07 -- the same scale as every deviation in this table, and larger than all but one of them (only hidden_l27's 2.14e-07 exceeds it). A cosine gate finer than about 1e-06 would be measuring the estimator's own summation error, not the port, and would fail on a thread-count change. The waveform's max_abs is the channel that keeps real resolution here: 9e-05 committed against 1.69e-05 measured, five times the deviation rounded up to one significant figure, computed by subtraction rather than accumulation and so free of that noise floor.

audio.pcm_freerun is NOT independent evidence on the 14 no-reference cases that matched the primary grid: the oracle's waveform there is already peak-normalised so the port's volume branch is the identity to the bit, and the free-run grid IS the replayed grid, which makes both sides byte-identical to audio.pcm's comparison -- the worst figures recorded for the two probes are the same numbers off the same case. Only the two clone cases compare something new (max_abs 2.83e-06 and 2.69e-06, against audio.pcm's 3.54e-06 and 4.34e-06), and omni-fast-mode is exempt on this channel because it matched an alternate grid the oracle has no waveform for. What the probe proves everywhere, and audio.pcm cannot, is that the codec is wired into the synthesis path at all.

One threshold this file will never carry: the token grid. structural_exactness for this family is EXACT equality of the committed 8 x T grid against the oracle's (17 greedy cases, measured 17/17 at commit time, one of them via the committed alternate grid); the validator fails any inexact grid unconditionally, before and independent of --check.

The grid is keyed on Quantization Profile, Execution Backend and stage, the layout tests/python/test_tolerance_coverage.py checks; F32 on CPU is the only measured cell, because Plan 2 is CPU-only and quantization is expected to be HARDER here than in any shipped family (a reference port measured token agreement collapsing to ~7% under an F16 generator; every future profile re-passes the exact-token gate or is not shipped).

replay.description: The oracle's grids replayed through the codec and the step-0 conditional forward compared against its probes; the greedy free-run grids compared exactly, outside this file.
replay.note:
Twenty cases: 17 greedy and 3 sampled. The sampled cases contribute the step-0 probes only -- their grids and waveforms are the public sampled path's claim, which Plan 3 makes -- so the two waveform probes above are measured over 20 and 16 cases respectively: audio.pcm covers every case, and audio.pcm_freerun covers 20 minus the 3 sampled cases (no greedy free-run) minus omni-fast-mode, which matched its alternate grid and is exempt from oracle parity on that channel.

Worst-case attribution, for the review this file records rather than for the gate: hidden_l27's max_abs of 0.0801 is omni-digits and is the largest absolute figure anywhere in the table, which is why the deep probes are cosine-gated -- the pre-norm outlier channels make max-abs useless as a threshold while the cosine holds at eight nines. The waveform's worst cosine is omni-medium-en and its worst max_abs omni-nonverbal, at 1.7e-05 on a signal peaking at 0.5.
